definitions.explanation: Describing soil or land that is rich in nutrients and well-suited for growing crops.

examples.japanese: この{土地|とち}は{肥沃|ひよく}だ。
{肥沃|ひよく}な{大地|だいち}で{農業|のうぎょう}が{盛|さか}んだ。
examples.english: Agriculture flourished on the fertile land.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}が{氾濫|はんらん}するたびに{栄養分|えいようぶん}が{運|はこ}ばれ、{流域|りゅういき}の{土壌|どじょう}は{非常|ひじょう}に{肥沃|ひよく}になった。
examples.english: Each time the river flooded, it carried nutrients, making the soil in the basin extremely fertile.

notes:
A な-adjective used almost exclusively to describe soil and land. The characters mean {肥|こ}える (to become rich/fat) + {沃|よく} (to irrigate/enrich). Common in geography, agriculture, and history texts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肥沃|ひよく}な{土地|とち}: fertile land
- {肥沃|ひよく}な{土壌|どじょう}: fertile soil
- {肥沃|ひよく}な{大地|だいち}: fertile earth
- {肥沃|ひよく}な{平野|へいや}: fertile plain
- {肥沃|ひよく}な{三日月|みかづき}{地帯|ちたい}: Fertile Crescent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {豊|ゆた}かな: rich, abundant — broader, not limited to soil
- {肥|こ}えた{土|つち}: rich soil — more colloquial way to say fertile soil
- {不毛|ふもう}: barren, infertile — the antonym
